title: iAgent: LLM Agent as a Shield between User and Recommender Systems

contributions.purpose: Provide benchmarks and a problem formulation for a new user-agent-platform recommendation paradigm in which an agent shields the user from the platform's algorithm (indirect exposure), addressing lack of user control, manipulation, echo chambers, and poor personalization for less-active users.
contributions.mechanism: Construct four recommendation datasets with user-driven free-text instructions (INSTRUCTREC) from existing Amazon, Goodreads, and Yelp data; introduce the Instruction-aware Agent (iAgent) that learns interests from free-text instructions and uses tools to fetch external knowledge as a domain expert.
contributions.evaluation: Four INSTRUCTREC datasets; iAgent alone already ranks best (EasyRec second-best) on HR@{1,3}, NDCG@3, MRR ranking metrics.
contributions.source_quote: To provide benchmarks for the new user-agent-platform paradigm, we construct four recommendation datasets with user-driven instructions, referred to as INSTRUCTREC, constructed from existing datasets such as Amazon, Goodreads, and Yelp. Building on this, we propose an Instruction-aware Agent (iAgent), designed to learn user interests from the provided free-text instructions while leveraging external knowledge to act as a domain-specific expert.

contributions.purpose: Learn from an individual user's feedback in isolation so recommendations are personalized and not dominated by other (active) users' behavior.
contributions.mechanism: Individual Instruction-aware Agent (i2Agent): a dynamic memory mechanism combining a profile generator (builds/maintains a user-specific profile from historical info and feedback) and a dynamic extractor (captures evolving profile/interests from the user's real-time instruction); optimized per individual user, not influenced by other users.
contributions.evaluation: Ablation/design validated on the four datasets; the dynamic memory + parser components drive the gains over EasyRec and enable diverse recommendations for both active and less-active users (see C3).
contributions.source_quote: We design Individual Instruction-aware Agent (i2Agent), incorporating a dynamic memory mechanism with a profile generator and dynamic extractor to further explore user interests and learn from user's individual feedback... i2Agent is optimized specifically for individual users and is not influenced by the interests or behaviors of other users, protecting the interests of less-active users.

contributions.purpose: Show i2Agent beats SOTA on ranking and additionally acts as a shield: mitigating echo-chamber/ad exposure and reducing bias against less-active users.
contributions.mechanism: Empirical comparison against three baseline classes (sequential: BERT4Rec/GRU4Rec/SASRec; instruction-aware: BM25/BGE-Rerank/EasyRec; recommendation agents: ToolRec/AgentCF) plus shield-specific metrics (filtered-Ads rate FR@{1,3,5,10}, popularity-weighted P-HR@3/P-MRR) and an active vs less-active user split.
contributions.evaluation: i2Agent achieves an average 16.6% improvement over the second-best baseline (EasyRec) across ranking metrics on four datasets; effectively removes inserted Ads items (echo-chamber mitigation) and improves performance for both active and less-active users.
contributions.source_quote: Empirical experiments on four datasets demonstrate that our i2 Agent consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches, achieving an improvement of up to 16.6% on average

self_declared_provenance.quote: Unlike the instructions in CRS (Sun & Zhang, 2018) and Webshop (Yao et al., 2022), the free-text instructions in INSTRUCTREC allow users to flexibly express their requirements beyond just product attributes.

Recently, some researchers have introduced LLM agents to simulate user behaviors, these approaches primarily aim to optimize platform-side performance, leaving core issues in recommender systems unresolved.
In our framework design, all recommendation models can be considered as components of the tools.

notes: Predominantly positive results (paper claims consistent SOTA-beating gains, 16.6% avg over EasyRec, plus echo-chamber and less-active-user benefits). Minor caveat noted by authors: active users tend to show POORER performance than less-active users because LLM quality degrades on longer texts (longer histories). No adversarial/negative benchmark results reported. Paper is under double-blind review (decision: reject).
